The early days of Tom and Jerry were great but they continued to try and milk the cat and mouse duo way to long and it lost its charm. Here is example of the good ones, and here is an example of a shitty one. The style in the latter example is so odd compared to the ones from the 50's I just cant watch those after seeing how great it once was.
There are two types of Tom and Jerry episodes good ones, and shitty ones.

Sadly, there is only one kind of Tom and Jerry cartoon, they just look different depending on how well they were fed.

Animation is a magic box that you stuff money into. The more money, the better the output. The old Tom and Jerry cartoons were intended as movie shorts, and had serious studio backing. Good artists, good writers, good everything. Ditto for the old Warner Brothers shorts.

It wasn't until TV matured enough to support it's own content creation that we realized how nice things were before. Hanna Barbera (and the other "made for TV" studios) pumped out content as best they could with tiny budgets. Terrible writing, repetitive frames, laugh tracks...

Even the "big budget" tv shows, Johnny Quest, Flinstones, etc. were weak sauce compared to the golden era of shorts.

The writing, animation, after a certain year completely changed, I can't remember the exact year but they went from being violent, and funny to a more politically correct parody of itself with shittier animation. I always figured it was because the animation/directing team changed so the original vision was lost. Similar to how the early stooges had a feel to them that the later ones didn't either due to cast changes, director changes, etc.

The original Hanna & Barbera run was from '40 to '57 (according to wikipedia). After that, it got dredged up and thrown into less competent hands with lower budgets. I'm not a fan of the Chuck Jones years, but I think he did the best he could with what he had. Everything after that is sort of hard to watch.

yes, those chuck jones ones are very rough to watch. I wonder how technology also affected the look and feel. I would guess by the early sixties they were starting to get some newer technology to help cut costs.
